header:
Date: 2026-01-28
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Recording: yes
Notes: Renewal/expansion check-in focused on EU private deployment path and contract extension (12 -> 18 months).
summary: Stonehaven is evaluating an 18-month renewal with a committed uplift for EU private deployment. Primary blockers: finalizing data residency requirements, KMS integration, and a short SLA addendum for latency-sensitive endpoints. Redwood to provide renewed pricing, SOW for private pilot, and a technical checklist for provisioning. Agreement to run a 2-week pilot in EU private region with baseline perf tests and KV cache tuning before final signature.
topics:
1) Renewal term options and pricing mechanics
2) EU private deployment architecture and AZ selection
3) Security (KMS/SSO/SOC2) and audit logs
4) Pilot scope: perf baselines, KV cache, throughput targets
5) Next steps and timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, appreciate it. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Tom (Stonehaven CTO): Hey Samir, Tom here, Priya, Eli, Jenna on our side.
[00:12] Priya (Stonehaven Head of Platform): Hi, thanks.
[00:14] Maya (Redwood SE): Hi all, Maya from the Redwood infra team. I'll be driving the pilot technical bits.
[00:18] Noah (Redwood CSM): Noah here, will help with the onboarding cadence.
[00:22] Tom: Cool. Goal for today is to align on the renewal ask and the EU private path, confirm what you need from us and the timeline.
[00:30] Samir: Exactly. High level — Stonehaven is up for renewal in March, you had mentioned wanting private deployment for EU due to residency. Customer requested an 18-month commitment with a capacity uplift, right?
[00:42] Priya: Yes, that’s the ask. We want to move sensitive traffic into a private VPC in eu-west-1, keep logs in-region. Also want an agreed latency SLO for a handful of low-latency routes.
[00:54] Eli (Security Lead): And KMS integration — keys cannot leave our control. We also have a SOC2 audit coming; need to make sure audit logs and retention meet our controls.
[01:05] Maya: Totally understood. For the KMS piece we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration and HSM-backed key wrapping in the private control plane. There are a couple of steps for access that we can share in the checklist.
[01:18] Jenna (DevOps): How mature is the private runtime for autoscaling? We run bursty inference loads at end of month and can't afford cold failure.
[01:28] Maya: Good question. The private runtime has the same autoscaler but you configure scaling policies. We recommend a baseline dedicated pool with burst capacity. For bursts we usually do warm pools + max scale to avoid cold starts. I'll include recommended instance types and warm pool sizing in the notes.
[01:44] [02:05] Samir: Let me step through renewal options we discussed in email: option A is 12 months with current capacity, option B is 18 months with 1.5x committed capacity and a discounted unit rate, option C is 24 months with larger uplift. Stonehaven seemed to prefer B. Any objections to going B plus a pilot to validate perf?
[02:22] Tom: B + pilot sounds good, we want to confirm performance and KV cache behavior in private before committing to full migration.
[02:30] Priya: Right, the KV cache and prefix caching are important for our token costs — if that regresses we could see a lot more spend.
[02:38] Maya: We can do a 2-week pilot in eu-west-1 private, replicate a subset of production traffic, and run perf baselines — latency P50/P95 and token cost per 1k requests. We'll instrument trace IDs to map to your app endpoints.
[02:52] Eli: On the SOC2 piece — do you provide evidence or a bridge for on-prem audits?
[02:58] Noah: We provide SOC2 reports and can arrange an SOC2 + ISO readout. For private deployments, we also offer extended audit logging and can keep logs in your cloud account depending on the setup.
[03:11] Eli: Okay. Also need to confirm if any PCI/PII data will be written to logs by default. We want minimal telemetry forwarded.
[03:19] Maya: Logging is configurable. By default we capture request metadata for observability, but you can disable or truncate payloads. We'll include the logging config options in the checklist.
[03:29] Priya: Sounds good. One item: can we control which AZs are used? We need data residency to be strictly in eu-west-1a and 1b only.
[03:39] Maya: We can restrict placement to specific AZs as part of the provisioning. There's an operational note on tradeoffs — limiting AZs reduces failover options but meets residency constraints. We'll record that and suggest a multi-AZ within those two.
[03:53] [04:20] Tom: Pricing question — the discounted rate for 1.5x commit reduces per-token unit, is that flat across models or differs by family?
[04:28] Samir: Discount tiers apply per model family. For large decoder models there’s a slightly different band; we’ll send a table. The renewal amendment will include per-model committed units and overage pricing.
[04:39] Oliver (Product): Do you have an approach for rolling back routes to hosted if private is unavailable? We cannot have total downtime.
[04:46] Maya: Yes, we support smart routing and automatic fallback to hosted variants. You can set policies per route: prefer private, fallback to hosted in same region, or fail closed. For the pilot we recommend fallback enabled.
[04:59] Priya: Is the fallback automatic or requires DNS change?
[05:03] Maya: It's handled by our control plane routing, no DNS changes required. Latency can increase on fallback depending on cross-region hops.
[05:13] Eli: About KMS: can Redwood see plaintext model inputs at any point?
[05:18] Maya: In private deployments data plane executes within your VPC and control plane can be configured not to retain payloads. With customer-managed KMS we never have access to unwrapped keys; however, telemetry traces may include masked IDs. We'll provide the exact threat model in the security doc.
[05:33] Tom: Good. For the pilot we need a baseline test profile. What's a pragmatic scope?
[05:38] Maya: Two parts: functional smoke tests (routing, keys, logging), then perf test with 5 representative endpoints at scaled qps. We'll aim to run a 48-72 hour sustained run at expected traffic and then some burst windows. We'll capture P50, P95, tail latencies and tokens-per-response.
[05:56] Priya: On instrumentation — we use Datadog, can you push traces to our account?
[06:01] Maya: Yes, we have an exporter; we can push traces to your Datadog API key or you can pull logs into your account. We'll include instructions.
[06:10] [06:45] Noah: Quick timeline alignment: if we start pilot week of 2026-02-08, run two weeks, then validation, we should be able to finalize amendment by mid-February. Does that work?
[06:56] Tom: That's aggressive but doable if we get checklist and infra details this week.
[07:02] Samir: I'll send the first draft of amendment and the pilot SOW by Tues 2026-02-02.
[07:08] Jenna: For the provisioning windows — what's typical lead time to spin private nodes?
[07:13] Maya: For eu-west-1 private it's typically 4-5 business days once we have AZ list and VPC peering/tunnels configured. If you want warm pools pre-provisioned that adds ~2 days.
[07:24] Jenna: Okay, we'll try to finalize VNets and peering details quickly.
[07:28] Eli: A compliance nuance: our legal wants a clause for data export within EU only. Can that be in the amendment?
[07:34] Samir: We can add a data residency addendum ensuring logs and storage are in-region and we won't replicate outside EU without prior approval. I'll flag legal to work with your counsel.
[07:42] Priya: One more technical: quantization/FP16 — do you support model variants in private runtime?
[07:49] Maya: Yes, the private runtime supports the same optimized kernels and selected quantized variants. We'll recommend a specific quantization profile for your workload; sometimes float16 gives best latency but int8 reduces cost. We'll test both in pilot.
[08:02] [08:30] Tom: Are there limitations on continuous batching that could affect tail latencies?
[08:36] Maya: Batching reduces cost but increases latency variance. We provide continuous batching knobs per route and per token budget; for those low-latency routes we'd set small max batch size and strict latency SLO. We'll show the config.
[08:50] Oliver: Who will run the perf tests? Redwood or Stonehaven?
[08:54] Maya: Jointly. We'll provide the harness and scripts; your team will run them in your environment with our observers. Noah will coordinate run windows.
[09:02] Priya: About logs — retention default is 90 days; can we set to 30 for this project?
[09:07] Samir: Yes, retention is configurable. We'll include options and implications for observability.
[09:13] Eli: Regarding SSO and RBAC — we need SAML with SCIM provisioning and granular roles for dev/prod.
[09:20] Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; role mapping can be customized. For private control plane we also support custom RBAC layers. We'll share the SSO integration guide.
[09:31] [10:05] Tom: Any risk of performance delta between hosted and private? Historically we've seen 5-10% variance when you control networking vs Redwood's public infra.
[10:15] Maya: There can be differences; in our experience with similar setups the private runtime in the same region is within ±3-8% for p95 depending on networking and instance types. We'll capture that in baseline. If it's outside agreed tolerance we can discuss remediation or temporary credit.
[10:31] Priya: Credits would be helpful.
[10:33] Samir: Noted — we'll include a clause in the amendment about remediation credits if pilot shows >15% regression on p95 for critical routes.
[10:44] Jenna: Ops question — who will own patching the private runtime nodes?
[10:48] Maya: Redwood manages the runtime binaries and initial config; customers can opt for an operational playbook for in-house teams. For security patches we push updates; for on-prem you'd schedule windows but in VPC model we coordinate rolling updates.
[11:01] Eli: For our SOC2, we'd like a runbook for incident response and change logs.
[11:06] Noah: We'll provide an incident response playbook and audit log access. We'll also provide the last 12 months of change logs for the control plane as part of security package.
[11:16] Tom: Good. One last commercial: can we get a price hold for 60 days after pilot completion? Our procurement needs time.
[11:24] Samir: Yes, we can offer a 60-day price lock post-pilot for the amendment if you sign within that window.
[11:30] Priya: That helps.
[11:33] [12:05] Oliver: Any competitive pricing notes — we are also talking to CloudCo AI and OpenServe. CloudCo offered slightly lower per-token for long-term but no private KMS support.
[12:16] Samir: Understood. Our differentiators are private KMS, routing, and observability which matters for your audit and SLOs.
[12:23] Eli: We'll send the SOC2 scope doc and SSO metadata after this call.
[12:27] Samir: Great, we'll take that and finalize the SOW.
[12:31] Noah: Quick recap of next steps: Samir sends amendment + pricing table by 2026-02-02; Maya sends private deployment checklist, KV cache tuning notes, and perf harness; Customer supplies AZ list, SSO metadata, and SOC2 scope by 2026-02-05; schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-02-08.
[12:48] Priya: Sounds good.
[12:51] Tom: Thanks all.
[12:53] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links.
[12:57] Jenna: Thanks.
[13:00] [42:00] <meeting ended>
